name: Fflur

attributes.attribute: fought Julius Caesar for her hand

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fflur was a Welsh heroine or goddess. The Welsh Triads mention this obscure figure. The hero Caswallawn held her in his affection. Caswallawn fought Julius Caesar to win her hand. Her name points toward the flower-maiden Blodeuwedd. A rivalry between two rulers suggests the goddess of Sovereignty. Yet Fflur's legend and its meaning are almost completely lost.

okr.objective: Fflur is an obscure Welsh heroine or goddess whose legend is almost completely lost.
key_results: Fflur appears in the Welsh Triads as the beloved of Caswallawn.
Caswallawn fought Julius Caesar for her hand.
Her name may link her to the flower-maiden Blodeuwedd.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
